$comment: Return attachments and the BIR eAFS system. Covers what must accompany each filing, through which channel (eAFS / eSubmission / at filing), by when, and what skipping it costs. The per-form matrix in perReturn drives the Forms page; the other blocks appear on the References register. Verified against the RMC 49-2020 → RMC 46-2026 issuance line on the date in meta.json.

value.what: BIR web facility (eafs.bir.gov.ph) for submitting the filed ITR, audited FS, and other required attachments as scanned PDFs
value.who: Any taxpayer, regardless of filing channel (eFPS, eBIRForms, or manual)
value.enrollment: Create an account with the taxpayer's TIN and an official email address; activate via the emailed link
value.fileFormat: PDF only, up to 4.8 GB per file
value.proof: System-generated Transaction Reference Number (TRN) plus the confirmation email. Keep both; they stand in for a manual 'Received' stamp

legalBasis: RMC 34-2025 & RMC 20-2026 (eAFS as the default channel for AITR attachments)
eafsSystem.notes: Introduced as an option in 2020; the annual filing RMCs now direct that AITR attachments 'shall be submitted electronically using the eAFS system'; over-the-counter submission to the LT Office/RDO/RCO is reserved for periods when a BIR advisory declares system unavailability (as happened April 2025 and May 2026).

annual.name: EAFS<TIN>ITRTY<MM><YYYY>
annual.contains: The filed AITR; for e-filers, the Filing Reference Number page (eFPS) or email Tax Return Receipt Confirmation (eBIRForms), plus proof of payment

annual.name: EAFS<TIN>AFSTY<MM><YYYY>
annual.contains: Statement of Management Responsibility; the audited FS with notes and independent auditor's report plus the certificate of the BIR-accredited independent CPA (audit required above ₱3M gross annual sales); or the unaudited FS / Account Information Form for filers below the threshold

annual.name: EAFS<TIN>OTHTY<MM><YYYY>-01 … -99
annual.contains: SAWT validation report, Forms 2307/2304/2316, duly approved tax debit memos, proofs of prior years' excess credits, foreign tax credits and other tax payments, CETI, and for amended returns the previously filed return with its proof of payment

annual.name: EAFS<TIN>RPTTY<MM><YYYY>
annual.contains: BIR Form 1709 (Related Party Transactions), for covered taxpayers

annual.name: EAFS<TIN>TCRTY<MM><YYYY>-01 … -99
annual.contains: Tax credit certificates and supporting documents

quarterly.name: EAFS<TIN>ITR<Q>Q<MM><YYYY>
quarterly.contains: The filed quarterly ITR (or FRN/email confirmation for e-filers)

quarterly.name: EAFS<TIN>OTH<Q>Q<MM><YYYY>-01 …
quarterly.contains: Scanned 2307s, SAWT confirmation, tax debit memos

value.conventions: <TIN> = 9-digit TIN without branch code; <MM> = month-end of the taxable year (12 for calendar year); <Q> = quarter number; split oversized groups across the numbered series

eafsFileGroups.notes: Example for TIN 123-456-789, CY2025: EAFS123456789ITRTY122025 · EAFS123456789AFSTY122025 · EAFS123456789OTHTY122025-01. The original 2020 naming without the month (…ITRTY2019) is superseded. The portal exposes three upload slots; place RPT/TCR files under the Other Attachments slot using the RMC-prescribed filenames.

itrAttachmentDeadline.value: Attachments to e-filed income tax returns are due within 15 days from the statutory filing deadline OR from the date of actual e-filing, whichever comes LATER: April 30 for calendar-year annual returns filed on time
itrAttachmentDeadline.notes: The BIR's default position is that the attachment deadline is not extended, but season RMCs can override it: for CY2025, RMC 30-2026 moved filing, payment AND attachments to May 15, 2026 (EO 110 energy emergency), RMC 39-2026 made May 15 the uniform eAFS deadline regardless of when the return was e-filed, and RMC 46-2026 gave a penalty-free grace to May 25, 2026 for eAFS system issues. Manually filed returns historically carried their attachments at filing; the current annual RMCs route those through eAFS as well.

value.audited: Gross annual sales/earnings/receipts above ₱3,000,000: books must be audited yearly by an independent CPA, and the annual ITR carries the audited FS with the auditor's report and Statement of Management Responsibility
value.unaudited: At or below ₱3,000,000 on ITEMIZED deductions: financial statements still attach to the annual return, just 'not necessarily audited' by a CPA (or the Account Information Form): the audit is waived below the threshold, the FS attachment is not
value.none: Individuals on the 8% option or OSD: no FS attach at all (1701A filers, and mixed-income earners on those regimes); records of gross sales/receipts must still be kept
value.corporations: Corporations submit FS with the annual return even on OSD (RR 16-2008), audited only above the ₱3M gross threshold for BIR purposes. The SEC's own AFS filing separately requires an audit unless total assets or total liabilities are below ₱600,000, where FS certified under oath by the treasurer/CFO suffice (RCC Sec 177)

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 232, as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN; audit threshold raised from ₱150,000 to ₱3,000,000)
BIR Form 1701/1702 guidelines (FS 'not necessarily audited' below the threshold, itemized deductions)
RR 16-2008 Sec 7 (OSD: individuals submit no FS, corporations still do)
Revised Corporation Code Sec 177 (SEC ₱600k treasurer-certification floor)
financialStatements.notes: The common trap: 'below ₱3M' does NOT mean 'no FS'. It means no CPA audit: itemized-deduction filers (and all corporations) still attach financial statements, unaudited, uploaded to the eAFS File 2 (AFS) group; only the 8% and OSD individual tracks skip the FS entirely. Audited FS become mandatory for BIR only when gross annual sales, earnings, receipts or output exceed ₱3,000,000 (NIRC Sec 232).

sawt.value: Any taxpayer claiming creditable withholding (Form 2307/2304 credits) on an income tax, VAT, or percentage tax return must submit the Summary Alphalist of Withholding Taxes with that return, generated as a .dat file with the BIR data entry module and emailed to esubmission@bir.gov.ph (or attached in eFPS), due when the return itself is due
sawt.notes: Applies to 1701Q/1702Q, 1701/1701A/1702, 2550Q and 2551Q whenever 2307 credits are claimed. The BIR's email validation report is the proof; it is what gets uploaded to eAFS as part of File 3 for annual (and optionally quarterly) ITRs. No SAWT, and the claimed credits are exposed to disallowance.

slsp.value: All VAT-registered taxpayers (no sales threshold) submit quarterly Summary Lists of Sales and Purchases/importations as RELIEF .dat files via eSubmission, due the 25th day after the close of the taxable quarter (30th for eFPS/LTS filers)
legalBasis: RR 16-2005 Sec 4.114-3, as amended by RR 1-2012
slsp.notes: Confirmed still required as of Aug 2026: e-invoicing/e-sales reporting under CREATE MORE (RR 11-2025) becomes mandatory for its first covered group only by Dec 31, 2026 and no issuance has retired the SLSP. Submit 'zero' lists for quarters with no transactions. Taxpayers already transmitting sales data to the EIS under RR 8-2022 are relieved of the sales list only; purchase/importation lists remain due. Penalty per unfiled list: ₱1,000 (capped ₱25,000/yr).

qapAlphalists.value: 1601-EQ and 1601-FQ carry the Quarterly Alphalist of Payees (QAP); 1604-C, 1604-E and 1604-F carry the annual employee/payee alphalists, all submitted through eSubmission (or eFPS) using the Alphalist Data Entry & Validation Module, currently v7.4 (with post-release patches)
legalBasis: RR 1-2014 & RMC 5-2014 (alphalist is integral to the return)
qapAlphalists.notes: The alphalist is an integral part of the return: a list that fails validation or doesn't conform to the format is deemed NOT received, the information return is treated as not validly filed, and the related expense deductions are at risk. QAP is due with the quarterly return (last day of the month after the quarter); annual alphalists with the 1604 series. v7.4 (RMC 15-2025) received patches in Nov 2025 and Jan 2026; re-validate .dat files after each patch; no v7.5 has issued as of Aug 2026.

employer2316Submission.value: Employers submit scanned copies of the duly signed 2316s of substituted-filing employees by February 28, accompanied by exactly two documents: the notarized sworn declaration (Annex C, RR 2-2015) and the Certification of the List of Employees Qualified for Substituted Filing (Annex F, RR 11-2018)
legalBasis: RR 2-2015, as amended by RR 16-2021 (scanned copies)
RMC 117-2021 (one mode per period; USB in absence of DVD-R)
RMC 29-2024 (only the two annexes may be required; both signatures mandatory)
employer2316Submission.notes: Accepted modes: eAFS upload, DVD-R, or USB, one mode per submission period. Scans must be legible and bear BOTH employer and employee signatures (e-signatures valid per RMC 29-2021; unsigned employee copies are no longer accepted per RMC 29-2024). DVD-R/USB files are named Surname_TIN_TaxablePeriod, arranged alphabetically. The deadline occasionally moves by RMC (CY2023's was extended to March 31, 2024).

form1709RelatedParty.value: BIR Form 1709 (Related Party Transactions) attaches to the annual ITR only for: (a) large taxpayers; (b) taxpayers enjoying incentives (ITH or preferential rate); (c) taxpayers reporting net operating losses for the current and two immediately preceding years; (d) related parties transacting with any of them
legalBasis: RMC 43-2021 & RMC 44-2021 (filing via eAFS RPT group or manually)
form1709RelatedParty.notes: Everyone else is exempt. Separate, higher thresholds trigger Transfer Pricing Documentation (kept on hand, not filed): gross sales > ₱150M AND total RPTs > ₱90M, or per-category RPTs above ₱60M (tangible goods) / ₱15M (services, interest, intangibles), or TPD was required the prior year.

cetiForRbes.value: Registered business enterprises claiming ITH, 5% SCIT, or enhanced deductions must secure the Certificate of Entitlement to Tax Incentives from their IPA (PEZA/BOI/etc.) before filing the annual ITR and attach it (eAFS Other Attachments group)
legalBasis: RMC 42-2026 (May 7, 2026 clarification on CETI submission with the AITR)
cetiForRbes.notes: Without the CETI the incentive claim on the return is at risk. Relevant to 1702-MX/1702-EX filers and BOI-registered individuals.

stampingRules.value: AFS submitted through eAFS need no BIR 'Received' stamping; the TRN and confirmation email are the proof. For attachments submitted manually, the 'RECEIVED' stamp goes on three pages only: the auditor's report, the balance sheet, and the income statement
legalBasis: RMC 49-2020 & RMC 82-2020 (TRN in lieu of stamp)
stampingRules.notes: Downstream, the SEC (eFAST) accepts the eAFS TRN/Confirmation Receipt in place of a BIR-stamped AFS.

value.standard: ₱1,000 per failure to file an information return, statement, list, or attachment, with an aggregate cap of ₱25,000 per calendar year (NIRC Sec 250)
value.microSmall: ₱500 per failure, capped at ₱12,500 per calendar year, for taxpayers classified micro or small under EOPT

lateAttachmentPenalties.notes: Late attachments do NOT make a timely-filed-and-paid return late: no 25% surcharge or interest attaches merely because attachments missed the window; the exposure is the Sec 250 penalty (collected in practice as a compromise penalty) plus practical risks: disallowance of 2307 credits never substantiated, alphalists deemed not received, audit flags, and open cases. Willful repeated non-compliance can escalate under Sec 255.

perReturn.notes: Everything is 'if applicable': a taxpayer with no attachments has nothing to upload. 1702-EX filers add their certificate of tax exemption; 1702-MX filers add the BOI/PEZA/IPA certificate and CETI. The per-form lists have stayed consistent from season to season (RMC 44-2023, 51-2024, 34-2025, then RMC 20-2026 for CY2025), and RMC 43-2021 remains the authority on the eAFS file groups; consult those annexes for the complete official wording.
